what: The panel teaches 'read it like a detective: last line first', but in a Node report the last line is the version footer. Chapter 12 lists this exact advice as a common wrong idea.
evidence: ch10 L499: "Read it like a detective: last line first." L508: "Last line first: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')". The captured stderr of crash_read.js ends with "Node.js v26.13.0", and the TypeError line is the 5th of 10 lines. ch12 notebook, Common wrong ideas: "'The last line of the report is the important one.' In Node it's the version footer. The Name: message line is in the middle."
fix: Change it to "Read it like a detective: the Name: message line first" (caption and list item). Use the same wording as ch12's recap, which says "Read it in order: the Name: message line, ...". The same phrase also appears in js ch5 L761, ch15 L100, ch22 L683 and ch23 L352/L752, so fix it across the book.

what: The suggested experiment can't show what it claims. If the default is null and the value is null, the output is null whether or not the default is used.
evidence: Lab: "Change the default on line 12 to understudy = null, then pass [\"Ada\", null] on the right. Does the default win? (It shouldn't: only undefined triggers a default.)" Ran in scratch on Node 22.23.4: `const [lead, understudy = null] = ["Ada", null]` prints "default: Ada null". `const [lead2, understudy2 = "Kit"] = ["Ada", null]` also prints "default: Ada null". Only the second version shows the rule.
fix: Rewrite as: "Keep the default \"Kit\" on line 12, but pass [\"Ada\", null] on the right. Does Kit step in? (No: null is a real value; only undefined triggers a default.)"

what: The question asks for the line that 'still crashes loudly if you misspell user', but all four options crash the same way on a misspelt name. The correct answer's own explanation admits it, so that test picks out nothing.
evidence: q: "Which line is safe for every user and still crashes loudly if you misspell user?" Correct option's why: "... a misspelt name is a ReferenceError either way." ch11 notebook: "A name that doesn't exist at all is still a ReferenceError: ?. protects against nullish values, not undeclared names." So user?.… options also throw ReferenceError.
fix: Replace the second test with one that tells the options apart, e.g. "...and still crashes loudly if user is ever undefined by mistake?" Then the plain dot after user is the deciding feature, and option 4's extra knock (and option 2's) hides that bug.

what: The Firefox wording is credited to MDN's error reference, but the MDN page the book links gives a different Firefox message.
evidence: ch11: "(according to MDN's error reference, Firefox reports a failed property read as can't access property \"city\", user.address is undefined)". Fetched MDN Errors/Cant_access_property, which now shows the page 'TypeError: "x" is (not) "y"'. Its Message block: 'TypeError: "x" is undefined (Firefox)', 'TypeError: "undefined" is not an object (Firefox)'. The string "can't access property" doesn't appear on that page, and the MDN error index has no entry with that title.
fix: Quote MDN's listed Firefox form ('"x" is undefined'), or drop the attribution: "Firefox and Safari word some of these differently; MDN's error reference lists each engine's wording" (ch12's sentence).

what: The link labelled 'TypeError: can't access property' goes to an MDN page now titled 'TypeError: "x" is (not) "y"'.

what: The prose says column 15 is 'the dot before row', but column 15 (and the caret) is the r of row. ch11 P21 has the same slip ("the caret under .city").

what: The Proofreader says line 2's { is never closed and that lines 4-6 are read as inside the if. In fact line 5's } closes the if, and it's the function's { on line 1 that's left open.
evidence: syntax_later.js: line 1 "function welcome(name) {", line 2 "  if (name === \"\") {", line 5 "}". Page: "The { on line 2 opens the if block, and nobody ever closes it. So I read on, thinking lines 4, 5 and 6 are all still inside it."
fix: Change it to: "The } on line 5 closes the if from line 2, so nothing is left to close the function from line 1. I read on to the end looking for it ...". Keep the exercise's answer (line 2 is where the missing brace belongs).

what: The page says the footprints 'start at Timeout._onTimeout, Node's timer', but that first frame is the reader's own arrow function (late_throw.js:3:11). What's missing is any frame for the try or the top level.
evidence: Captured stderr: "at Timeout._onTimeout (file:///home/you/javascript-ch12/late_throw.js:3:11)", then "at listOnTimeout (node:internal/timers…)" and "at process.processTimers (node:internal/timers…)". Page: "Look at the footprints: they start at Timeout._onTimeout, Node's timer, not at line 1."

panel: notebook: Under the hood (The call stack and the trace)
what: The example given for 'an error made with new Error on line 4' is panel 30's third road, but that error is a TypeError the engine created on line 5.
